text: #359's in-place proof in the gate, for @gitdek's ratification, in place of D-0223, D-0250 and D-0251 after #359's second review. verify.Check and verify.Run admit a check that selects an in-place proof of a Python function only beside conformance on the same function; the direct Python check refuses it, since it returns no proof. verify.Check refuses, before any tool runs, what the function's own source shows the gate can't prove: what the verifier input can't preserve of the function, an async function, a decorator, Pure included, since conformance binds only undecorated functions, Assume, which has Nagini take a fact nothing proves, and a contract that couldn't run as Nagini reads it. The module runs with Invariant's runtime stand-in for nagini_contracts, so Python calls each contract statement where it stands and evaluates its arguments then: a postcondition on entry, which Nagini reads at exit, and an Implies' consequent whether or not its antecedent holds. So Nagini's names may appear only in contract statements, Requires, Ensures, Exsures, Decreases, Assert and Invariant, whose calls must bind as the stand-in takes them, and their arguments may hold only names, literals and tuples of them, Result(), Old() and the stand-in's other names, comparisons, and, or and not, conditional expressions, +, - and *, unary operators, and calls of len, abs and isinstance with a type's name, which the pinned Nagini models and which can't fail on the types it checks. min and max are left out, since their one-argument form fails on an empty list where Nagini only requires one that isn't. A membership test of Result() needs a tuple it lists, since a string or bytes can't hold Result()'s value, and a contract reads a local only where every path to it binds the local first. Everything else is refused: a subscript, a division, a floor division, a modulo, a power, a shift, a bitwise operator, an attribute read, any other call, a display, a comprehension and a lambda among it. Result() returns an inert value that answers every allowed operator, reflected forms included, made afresh, class and all, on every call. Once the session has staged the application and selected its dependency image, before any test, conformance, backing test or Nagini runs, the gate refuses what depends on the rest of the application: a binding, a trusted contract or a production source the verifier input can't stand for, and a nagini_contracts that isn't Invariant's stand-in. The application must ship the stand-in at its root, exactly its __init__.py and contracts.py and nothing else in that package, and no other nagini_contracts anywhere else, which a change to the import path could load instead; a selected function may read only the names the stand-in's __all__, a tuple, exports. The bytes alone don't settle what the stand-in binds when the module runs, so the scan for writes protects nagini_contracts, its contracts module and the builtins as it does the function's module: production code may read their attributes, and may not write them, reach them through sys.modules, by name or through a patcher, read their __dict__ or hand them to a call, vars and reload included. The scan also refuses, anywhere in production code, running or compiling code from a string, reaching modules through inspect.getmodule or gc, reading or naming in a string __globals__, f_globals, f_builtins or __builtins__, and writing a function's __code__, __defaults__ or __kwdefaults__. What the application's dependencies run, and calls whose function is computed, stay assumed, as D-0247 says. After the application's tests, conformance and backing tests, the gate runs the pinned Nagini from its recipe on each input, apart from the application's image, records each attempt in the application report and attributes its result as component proof evidence. A proof qualifies only as an effective guarantee: the function proved from its original bytes, with no error and nothing it reached unaccounted for, every trusted contract it assumed tested, and conformance on the same function passing in the same session against the same source bytes, since the collector binds what conformance observes to that very staged declaration. A proof that doesn't qualify fails the gate. One Nagini verified is marked unqualified in the report, which later attribution keeps, and receipts call it not qualified and leave it out of the proved count. A receipt counts an in-place result, which a tool pin of its own marks, only beside the attempt that pin names, and shows each proof as holding only on the condition that its trusted contracts hold, which tests support and nothing proves. Fingerprints bind each attempt's input, recipe and result, never its local image, its command, Nagini's output or its timing. A proof covers only the selected function's own body: no dependency, no unselected function and not the whole application.
